INSTRUMENT MISMATCH (SKILL.md Step 3b): the table is named/described as a "10-item financial security scale", but its ten items secf_1m..secf_10m are the study's DEPRESSION measure -- the CES-D-10. Evidence from the study's own S1 SAS file: rowSums(secf_1m..secf_10m) equals its variable `dpsscore` exactly for all 371 respondents (max |diff| = 0), `dps` (labelled 'depression') equals (dpsscore >= 10) exactly (209/371, 56.3%), and the paper states 'Self-reported depressive symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiological Studies-Depression Revised 10 (CES-D-10)... The range of the 10-item scale is 0 to 30 and the recommended cutoff score of >=10 was used'. The live totals reproduce all of that (mean 11.404, SD 6.199, range 0-30, 56.33% >= 10). The financial-health variables the table name refers to are different columns of the same file (fingoal, budget, directdeposit, spendsav, latefee, checking, savings, owemoney, utilshut, noheat) and are NOT in this IRW table. Extracted against what the data actually is, per Step 3b; dictionary Description and the table name both need correcting.

Anchors ship REVERSED for secf_5m and secf_8m. The CES-D-10's two positive-affect items ('I felt hopeful about the future', 'I was happy') are stored already reverse scored: both correlate POSITIVELY (+0.09..+0.49) with the seven other negatively worded items, and the plain rowSum reproduces the authors' own dpsscore. So for those two items resp 3 = 'rarely or none of the time' and resp 0 = 'most or all of the time'. Every other item ships the anchors in the printed 0-3 order.

DATA CAVEAT: secf_4m ('I felt that everything I did was an effort') is detached from the scale in this sample -- item-rest r = 0.07 against 0.27-0.73 for the other nine, and it is the only item the two positive-affect items correlate negatively with (-0.18, -0.08). It is also the most endorsed item (mean 1.679). Its position rests on the canonical CES-D-10 order plus that endorsement rank, not on any correlational signal; it is the weakest of the ten assignments.
